lesson_title: Conversions and Estimating: Paint Tins, Oven Dials and the Second Trip
hook_text: The label says 5 litres covers 30 square metres. Your wall is 51. Here's how to buy paint exactly once.
clip_script: Five litres covers thirty square metres. So one litre covers six. Your wall is fifty-one square metres and it wants two coats — that's a hundred and two square metres of covering. Divide by six: seventeen litres. And here's where school maths ends and real life begins. Nobody sells seventeen litres. The shop has five-litre tins at R465 and a twenty-litre drum at R1 680. Four tins is twenty litres for R1 860. The drum is the same twenty litres for R1 680. Same paint. R180 apart. So the answer isn't seventeen litres. The answer is: buy the drum. And while you're in the kitchen — the old recipe says 400 degrees, but that's Fahrenheit. Take the 32 off FIRST: 368. Times five: 1 840. Divide by nine: 204,44. Set your oven to 200. Take the 32 off first coming down, put it on last going up. Get that order wrong and the cake comes out a brick.
visual_style: A hardware aisle and a kitchen counter intercut — tins stacking up against a single drum, a wall flooding with colour, an oven dial spinning from Fahrenheit to Celsius, price tags flipping to reveal the R180 gap.
mood: Practical, warm, slightly conspiratorial — insider knowledge about never wasting money.
pacing: Brisk through the paint arithmetic, a held beat on the price comparison, deliberate on the temperature steps.
